question:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/213ec2507211ba84c9b69be2f86ddbc4af76476380f8c255bd1459fdba8ef70a.png] 

In the figure AB is parallel to CD and BE is parallel to FH. What is ∠FHE equal to?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two sets of lines are **parallel** (AB ∥ CD and BE ∥ FH), the angle formed between the first pair is always equal to or supplementary to the angle formed between the second pair due to the **Corresponding Angles Postulate**.

Since the inclination of **BE** relative to **AB** is the same as the inclination of **FH** relative to **CD**, the angles are **identical**.

∠FHE = Given Angle = 110°.

**∴ The correct answer is 110°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **AB ∥ CD** and **BE ∥ FH**.

**Formula Used:** Properties of **Parallel Lines** (Corresponding and Alternate Interior Angles).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4cacb6ebd4fe6e9be064b9e74638c73c45992c368d07eb59fc8fa1b764c26796.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Consider **AB ∥ CD**. If a transversal **BH** intersects them, then the **Alternate Interior Angles** are equal.

⇒ Similarly, since **BE ∥ FH**, the angle these lines make with any transversal or any other set of parallel lines remains **constant**.

⇒ In the given geometric configuration, ∠ABE corresponds to ∠FHD.

⇒ By the property of **Corresponding Angles** between two pairs of parallel lines:

⇒ ∠FHE = 110°.

**∴ The correct answer is 110°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Corresponding Angles

When a transversal intersects two parallel lines, the angles in the same relative position at each intersection are equal.

Alternate Interior Angles

Angles situated between the parallel lines on opposite sides of the transversal are always equal (∠3 = ∠5).

Consecutive Interior Angles

Also known as co-interior angles, these are located on the same side of the transversal and sum up to 180°.</p
